problem: Problems in loop theory and quasigroup theory consider generalizations of groups
source: List of problems in loop theory and quasigroup theory
missing_details: Exact statements of each individual open problem (e.g. existence of infinite simple paramedial quasigroups)
Formal definitions of quasigroups and loops (binary operation, division property, identity)
Definitions of specialized terms: nucleus, isotopy, multiplication group, inner mapping group, Bol loop, Moufang loop, Osborn loop, alternative loop
Notation for elements, operations, quotient structures, and order constraints
Contextual conditions (finite vs infinite cases, relative primality of orders)
Origins and proposers of each problem (conference, year)
Known partial results or solved cases
refined_question: List and precisely formulate each of the open problems in loop theory and quasigroup theory that generalize properties of groups, providing for each problem (1) the necessary definitions of quasigroups and loops, (2) all specialized terms and notation (e.g. nucleus, isotopy, multiplication group, inner mapping group, varieties, Bol and Moufang identities), (3) the exact statement including domain constraints (finite or infinite, order conditions), and (4) the provenance (conference and proposer).
justification: The original name merely indicates that open problems exist in the area of loops and quasigroups as generalizations of groups, without specifying any particular question or providing definitions, notation, conditions, or provenance. To make the inquiry self-contained and precise, one must enumerate each problem with its full technical statement, definitions, and context. This refined formulation faithfully captures the content and scope of the canonical source without broadening or omitting any of its constraints.
